extracted.intended_audience: people researching philanthropic grantmaking, journalists, policymakers, and scholars interested in the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation's programs and funding policies
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of grantmaking practices, program criteria, and funding-policy standards described on the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation Wikipedia page. Focuses on explicit grant conditions, selection criteria for scholarships/prizes, programmatic targeting, and stated investment/funding policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Findings-sharing condition for HIV research grants
rubrics_metrics.description: HIV Research: The foundation donated a total of $287 million to various HIV/AIDS researchers. The money was split between 16 different research teams across the world, on the condition that the findings are shared amongst the teams.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding was explicitly conditioned on shared dissemination of results among recipient teams (example given for HIV research funding).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholarship selection — Gates Cambridge (outstanding graduate students)
rubrics_metrics.description: Gates Cambridge Scholarships: donation to help outstanding graduate students from the U.S. and around the world to study at the University of Cambridge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program is highly competitive (about 0.3% of applicants selected); approximately 100 new graduate students receive funding each year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholarship selection — Gates Millennium Scholars (high-achieving minority students)
rubrics_metrics.description: Gates Millennium Scholars: administered by the United Negro College Fund, the foundation donated $1.5 billion for scholarships to high achieving minority students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targeted to high-achieving minority students; program scale and administration by UNCF are emphasized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholar selection criteria — University Scholars Program (financial need and interdisciplinary potential)
rubrics_metrics.description: University Scholars Program: provides full scholarships; scholars are chosen based on financial need and potential for interdisciplinary academic interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program includes seminars, mentoring by graduate/professional scholars, and selection each spring from new applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholarship obligation — William H. Gates Public Service Law Program
rubrics_metrics.description: William H. Gates Public Service Law Program: awards five full scholarships annually to the University of Washington School of Law; scholars commit to working in relatively low-paying public service legal positions for at least the first five years following graduation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The scholarship includes an explicit post-graduation service commitment as a condition of the award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prize/grant design criterion — Next-Generation Condom
rubrics_metrics.description: Next-Generation Condom: foundation gave $100,000 to 11 applicants in November 2013 to develop an improved condom that 'significantly preserves or enhances pleasure, in order to improve uptake and regular use.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial awards to multiple applicants ($100k each) with further grants (up to $1 million) available to successful projects; the solicitation included an explicit performance/usage-oriented design requirement (enhanced pleasure to improve uptake).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restricted-use / project-exclusive grant terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Example: a Gates Foundation grant to the Discovery Institute was described as 'exclusive to the Cascadia project' and 'may not be used for the institute's other activities, including promotion of intelligent design.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants may include express restrictions limiting how recipients can use funds (project-specific exclusivity clauses).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and editorial-independence practice for grantees
rubrics_metrics.description: The foundation has said it lists all its grants publicly and does not enforce any rules for content among its grantees, who have editorial independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two stated practices: public listing of grants (transparency) and absence of content controls on grantee editorial work (editorial independence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding policy — avoid direct abortion funding; focus on voluntary family planning
rubrics_metrics.description: The foundation decided not to fund abortion, focusing instead on family planning and contraception 'in order to avoid conflation of abortion and family planning.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This represents an explicit normative funding policy guiding which reproductive-health activities the foundation supports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investment policy — prioritize maximizing financial return (with shareholder engagement)
rubrics_metrics.description: The foundation trust invests undistributed assets with the exclusive goal of maximizing the return on investment; as a result, its investments include companies criticized for their practices. The foundation uses voting rights to influence company practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The foundation considered, then canceled, a review of investments for social responsibility and publicly defended investing for maximum return while attempting to influence corporate behavior through shareholder votes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Price-reduction / affordability targets in procurement/partnership agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Cheaper high-tech tuberculosis (TB) test: the foundation, with partners, finalized an agreement to reduce the cost of a commercial TB test (Cepheid's Xpert MTB/RIF) from $16.86 to $9.98.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A funding/partnership objective explicitly tied to lowering unit cost of diagnostics to improve access and replace older techniques (smear microscopy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeting products and delivery for low-/middle-income or high-burden countries
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple grants specify target users/markets: e.g., Aeras Global TB Vaccine Foundation funding to develop and license a vaccine for use in high-burden countries; Group B streptococcus vaccine funding for distribution in developing countries; monoclonal antibody delivery methods targeted for low- and middle-income countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programmatic funding criteria prioritize applicability, licensing, delivery and distribution that meet the needs of LMICs or high-burden settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority for rapid deployability of epidemic vaccines (CEPI/epidemic preparedness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (CEPI): aims to develop vaccines against known infectious disease threats that could be deployed quickly to contain outbreaks before they become global health emergencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding emphasis on speed-to-deployment and outbreak containment capability as a desired attribute of candidate vaccines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for commercialization/partnership pathways for research outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: The foundation urged the University of Oxford to find a large company partner to get its COVID-19 vaccine to market (an action that drew criticism and affected earlier commitments about donating rights).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrates a practice/expectation that funded biomedical research may be steered toward partnerships with commercial manufacturers to achieve market access and distribution — a de facto criterion in some programs.
